From:           Alan Blind
To:             Petition Resource
Cc:             Dennis Galvin; PalisadesRestartProject
Subject:        [External_Sender] 10 CFR 2.206 Petition and Request for Immediate Action – Palisades Nuclear Plant
Date:           Sunday, October 4, 2026 11:02:07 AM
Attachments:    Petition for NRC Action Palisades Nuclear Plant Refueling.pdf




NRC Executive Director for Operations:

Attached is my petition pursuant to 10 CFR 2.206 concerning the recent fuel-handling event at
the Palisades Nuclear Plant and the suspension of reactor core refueling operations.

The petition raises three principal issues requiring NRC review before core refueling
resumes: (1) determination of the cause, extent of condition, and corrective actions associated
with the fuel assembly that tilted after placement and disengagement of the fuel-handling-
machine grapple; (2) NRC inspection and independent verification of the 10 CFR 50.59
review associated with the recently installed Refueling Machine and upgraded Fuel Handling
System, including a broader review of the restart modification program if substantive
deficiencies are identified; and (3) determination of whether fatigue, work schedules,
workload, staffing, or other human-performance factors contributed to the event, including
review of the August 12, 2026 NRC-approved exemption from the normal work-hour
requirements of 10 CFR 26.205.

In addition to the relief requested in the petition, I respectfully request immediate action
while the NRC processes this petition, pursuant to the immediate-action provisions of NRC
Management Directive 8.11, “Review Process for 10 CFR 2.206 Petitions.”

Specifically, I request that the NRC take immediate action to prevent Palisades Energy, LLC
from resuming reactor core refueling operations while the NRC evaluates the matters raised in
the petition.

Management Directive 8.11 provides for NRC consideration of requests for immediate action
separately from the normal processing and ultimate disposition of a 10 CFR 2.206 petition.
This procedure is particularly relevant where the activity that is the subject of the petition
could occur before the NRC completes its review, thereby diminishing the effectiveness of the
relief requested.

There is directly relevant NRC precedent for such treatment. The case was Indian Point Unit
2, on a petition dated December 4, 2000, submitted by Deborah Katz et al. (Citizens
Awareness Network). One of the requested actions was that NRC keep Indian Point Unit 2
offline until alleged underlying management problems were analyzed and corrected.

I was Vice President Nuclear at Indian Point at the time and was therefore directly familiar
with the circumstances surrounding that proceeding.

The NRC's status report states:

      “With the SG replacement having been completed at IP2, and the licensee in the
      process of restart, the PRB convened a meeting on December 20, 2000, to
      consider the Immediate Action request related to plant restart.”
 PETITION PURSUANT TO 10 CFR 2.206
Palisades Nuclear Plant
Docket No. 50-255

I. REQUEST FOR ENFORCEMENT ACTION
Pursuant to 10 CFR 2.206, I request that the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission institute a
proceeding pursuant to 10 CFR 2.202 and issue an Order prohibiting Palisades Energy, LLC
from resuming reactor core refueling operations at the Palisades Nuclear Plant without
prior NRC authorization until the NRC determines that::

     1.   The cause of the fuel assembly tilting after placement and disengagement of the fuel-
          handling-machine grapple has been determined;

     2.   The extent of condition has been established, including whether the same condition could
          affect other fuel assemblies, core locations, fuel-handling equipment, or subsequent
          refueling operations;

     3.   Corrective actions necessary to preclude recurrence have been completed;

     4.   The Refueling Machine and applicable Fuel Handling System interlocks, load-limiting
          devices, travel-limiting devices, grapple mechanisms, indications, controls, and other
          protective features have been demonstrated to perform their design functions;

     5.   The procedures and acceptance criteria used to establish that a fuel assembly is properly
          positioned, fully seated, stable, and suitable for grapple disengagement are adequate;

     6.   The requirements of 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion XVI, “Corrective Action,”
          have been satis ed with respect to the event;

     7.   The condition that resulted in the tilted fuel assembly has been evaluated against the
          Palisades licensing and design basis, including FSAR Revision 36, Section 9.11;

     8.   The NRC has inspected and independently veri ed the adequacy of the 10 CFR 50.59
          screening and, if applicable, evaluation performed for the recently installed Refueling
          Machine and associated Fuel Handling System modi cations;

     9.   If the NRC identi es substantive ndings concerning the Refueling Machine modi cation
          or its 10 CFR 50.59 review, the NRC has determined whether those ndings warrant an
          Event and Causal Factors Inspection, Special Inspection, or other focused inspection of a
          risk-informed sample of signi cant modi cations performed during the Palisades restart
          program;




                      fi
                 fi         fi
     fi
fi                                 fi   fi              fi             fi
             10. The NRC has determined whether acute or cumulative fatigue, work schedules,
                workload, staf ng, schedule pressure, supervision, or other human-performance factors
                caused or contributed to the fuel assembly tilting event; and

            11. The NRC has independently determined that there is reasonable assurance that
                resumption of reactor core refueling operations will not result in recurrence of the
                condition.

          In addition, the petitioner requests that the NRC suspend the August 12, 2026 exemption from
          the normal work-hour requirements of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(3) and (d)(7), as applicable to
          Operations personnel participating in reactor core refueling activities, pending NRC
          determination of whether fatigue or human-performance factors caused or contributed to
          the event.

          The requested Order should remain in effect until these conditions have been satis ed and the
          NRC documents its basis for permitting reactor core refueling operations to resume.



          II. REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS AT
          ISSUE
          A. 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion XVI —
          Corrective Action
          The principal regulatory requirement implicated by the fuel-handling event is 10 CFR Part 50,
          Appendix B, Criterion XVI, “Corrective Action.”

          Criterion XVI requires that measures be established to assure that conditions adverse to quality,
          including failures, malfunctions, de ciencies, deviations, defective material and equipment, and
          nonconformances, are promptly identi ed and corrected.

          For signi cant conditions adverse to quality, Criterion XVI additionally requires measures to
          assure that the cause of the condition is determined and corrective action is taken to preclude
          repetition.

          The tilted-fuel-assembly event presents a condition potentially adverse to quality involving
          equipment and activities described in the Palisades FSAR as providing for the safe handling of
          nuclear fuel.

          The event resulted in suspension of normal reactor core refueling operations and initiation of a
          root-cause evaluation.




                                                                              fi
                                   fi
                              fi
     fi
fi
      Accordingly, the event should be treated as a potentially signi cant condition adverse to quality
     until the NRC determines otherwise.

     Resumption of reactor core refueling operations before the cause is determined, the extent of
     condition established, and corrective actions suf cient to preclude recurrence are implemented
     would raise a substantial question regarding compliance with Criterion XVI.

     B. 10 CFR 50.59 — Recently Modi ed Fuel Handling System
     A separate regulatory question concerns 10 CFR 50.59, “Changes, tests, and experiments.”

     Public statements attributed to Holtec concerning the Palisades restart establish that the Fuel
     Handling System underwent a signi cant modi cation shortly before reactor core refueling
     operations commenced.

     On July 3, 2026, World Nuclear News reported that Holtec announced successful completion of
      nal major restart projects at Palisades, including the installation and testing of a new state-of-
     the-art fuel handling machine, completing the upgraded fuel handling system.

     The Refueling Machine is equipment speci cally described in Palisades FSAR Revision 36,
     Section 9.11.4.3 as part of the Fuel Handling System.

     The NRC should therefore independently inspect the modi cation package for this recently
     installed equipment and determine whether the licensee's evaluation under 10 CFR 50.59
     adequately addressed the modi cation of the Refueling Machine and Fuel Handling System
     described in the FSAR.

     The petitioner does not presently assert that the licensee's 10 CFR 50.59 evaluation was
     inadequate.

     Rather, the subsequent occurrence of an abnormal fuel-handling event involving the newly
     installed equipment provides a reasonable basis for NRC inspection of that evaluation before the
     equipment is again used for reactor core refueling.

     C. 10 CFR Part 26 — Fitness for Duty and Work-Hour
     Controls
     A third regulatory issue concerns the NRC's August 12, 2026 exemption from the work-hour
     requirements of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(3) and (d)(7) for Operations personnel.

     The purpose of Subpart I of 10 CFR Part 26 is to ensure that worker fatigue does not
     compromise the ability of individuals to perform their duties safely and competently. The NRC
     expressly recognized that purpose when evaluating the Palisades exemption. ML26216A290




                                                          fi
                                                     fi
                                                fi
                                           fi
                                      fi
                                 fi
                          fi
                     fi
fi
 The NRC ultimately permitted Operations personnel to use the less restrictive outage minimum-
days-off requirements beginning with core load for up to 60 days or until grid connection,
whichever occurred rst. ML26216A290

The fuel assembly tilting event occurred during the core-loading activities to which this
exemption applied.

Accordingly, whether fatigue or human-performance factors contributed to the event is relevant
both to the root-cause evaluation and to the continued validity of the NRC ndings supporting
the exemption.



III. PALISADES FSAR DESIGN BASIS
Palisades FSAR Revision 36, Chapter 9, Section 9.11 is titled “Fuel Handling and Storage
Systems.”

Section 9.11.1 establishes the fundamental design function of the Fuel Handling System:

“The Fuel Handling System (Table 9-19) provides for the safe handling and storage of fuel under
all foreseeable conditions…”

The FSAR further states:

“The design and construction of the system includes interlocks, travel and load limiting devices
and other protective measures to minimize the possibility of mishandling or equipment
malfunction that could cause damage to the fuel and potential ssion product release.”

Thus, the Palisades design basis does not rely solely upon operator performance to accomplish
safe fuel handling.

The Fuel Handling System incorporates engineered protective features, including interlocks and
travel and load limiting devices, intended to minimize the possibility of fuel mishandling or
equipment malfunction.

FSAR Section 9.11.4.3 describes the Refueling Machine as a traveling bridge and trolley
spanning the refueling cavity, with controls located on a console on the Refueling Machine
trolley.

FSAR Table 9-19 speci es a fuel assembly weight of approximately 1,500 pounds.

These FSAR provisions provide the design-basis reference against which both the fuel-handling
event and the recently installed Refueling Machine should be evaluated.




                                                            fi
                                               fi
          fi
     fi
 IV. THE FUEL-HANDLING EVENT
The known event presents a condition fundamentally different from the intended result of normal
reactor core refueling.

The expected sequence is:

Fuel assembly under positive control → assembly positioned over designated core location
→ assembly lowered into location → assembly reaches its required nal position → stable/
seated condition established → grapple disengaged → assembly remains upright in its
intended core location.

Instead, the reported sequence was:

Fuel assembly placed → fuel-handling-machine grapple disengaged → fuel assembly tilted
from its upright position → reactor core refueling operations stopped → root-cause
evaluation initiated.

The assembly therefore reached a condition in which positive control through the grapple had
been relinquished but the assembly did not remain in its intended stable, upright con guration.

The presently available information does not establish why.

Possible causes may include the fuel assembly itself, incomplete seating, interference, improper
positioning, core-support geometry, Refueling Machine positioning, hoist or load indication,
equipment malfunction, procedural inadequacy, operator action, fatigue or human performance,
or another condition.

This petition does not ask the NRC to presume which explanation is correct.

It requests that the NRC determine the cause before permitting continuation of an activity that
could reproduce the condition.



V. SIGNIFICANCE OF THE FSAR-
DESCRIBED PROTECTIVE FEATURES
The event raises a particularly important question concerning the FSAR statement that the Fuel
Handling System contains:

“interlocks, travel and load limiting devices and other protective measures.”




                                                                      fi
                                                         fi
      Those features are expressly described as minimizing the possibility of mishandling or
     equipment malfunction that could cause damage to fuel.

     Nevertheless, the fuel-handling evolution progressed through placement of the assembly and
     disengagement of the grapple before the assembly tilted.

     The NRC should therefore determine what indications or protective features were applicable
     during nal placement of the assembly and immediately before disengagement of the grapple.

     The NRC should determine, at a minimum:

       •  what Refueling Machine load indication existed during lowering and placement;
       •  whether load indication demonstrated transfer of assembly weight from the hoist/grapple
          to the reactor core support structure;
       •  whether underload, overload, slack-cable, travel, elevation, or similar protective features
          were provided;
       •  whether any applicable interlock or protective feature actuated;
       •  whether any applicable protective feature failed to actuate or was bypassed;
       •  what criteria were required to be satis ed before disengagement of the grapple;
       •  whether the assembly reached its required elevation before grapple disengagement;
       •  whether the Refueling Machine was correctly aligned with the designated core location;
       •  whether interference or abnormal resistance occurred during lowering; and
       •  whether the operator received any anomalous load, elevation, position, or other indication
          before releasing the assembly.
     FSAR Table 9-19 speci es a fuel assembly weight of approximately 1,500 pounds.

     The NRC should determine what load indication, mechanical indication, procedural veri cation,
     or other means is relied upon to demonstrate that a fuel assembly has transitioned from being
     supported by the Refueling Machine to being properly supported and stable in its intended core
     location before the grapple is disengaged.



     VI. NRC REVIEW OF THE REFUELING
     MACHINE MODIFICATION AND 10 CFR
     50.59 EVALUATION
     The fact that the Refueling Machine and Fuel Handling System were recently upgraded makes
     review of the modi cation particularly important.

     Holtec publicly characterized the work as installation and testing of a new state-of-the-art fuel
     handling machine that completed the upgraded fuel handling system.

     The Refueling Machine is equipment speci cally described in Palisades FSAR Revision 36 as
     part of the Fuel Handling System.




                                                                               fi
                                 fi
                           fi
                fi
           fi
fi
                     Under 10 CFR 50.59, changes to the facility or procedures as described in the FSAR must be
                    screened and, when applicable, evaluated to determine whether prior NRC approval is required.

                    The NRC should obtain and inspect the complete modi cation package for the new Refueling
                    Machine and associated Fuel Handling System changes, including:

                      •    the 10 CFR 50.59 screening;
                      •    any 10 CFR 50.59 evaluation;
                      •    modi cation design speci cations;
                      •    design-basis and licensing-basis reviews;
                      •    calculations and engineering evaluations;
                      •    vendor technical information;
                      •    Refueling Machine load and position monitoring design;
                      •    interlock design and setpoints;
                      •    grapple control and release logic;
                      •    bridge, trolley, and hoist positioning requirements;
                      •    factory and site acceptance testing;
                      •    post-modi cation testing;
                      •    preoperational testing;
                      •    procedure changes;
                      •    operator training associated with the new equipment; and
                      •    con guration-control changes to the FSAR and other licensing-basis documents.
                    The NRC should speci cally determine whether the §50.59 review adequately evaluated whether
                    the modi cation:

                      1.   resulted in more than a minimal increase in the frequency of occurrence of an accident
                           previously evaluated in the FSAR;

                      2.   resulted in more than a minimal increase in the likelihood of occurrence of a malfunction
                           of a structure, system, or component important to safety previously evaluated in the
                           FSAR;

                      3.   resulted in more than a minimal increase in the consequences of an accident previously
                           evaluated in the FSAR;

                      4.   resulted in more than a minimal increase in the consequences of a malfunction of a
                           structure, system, or component important to safety previously evaluated in the FSAR;

                      5.   created a possibility for an accident of a different type than any previously evaluated in
                           the FSAR;

                      6.   created a possibility for a malfunction of a structure, system, or component important to
                           safety with a different result than previously evaluated in the FSAR;

                      7.   resulted in a design-basis limit for a ssion product barrier being exceeded or altered; or




                                                            fi
                                         fi
                                fi
                           fi
               fi
          fi
     fi
fi
                                8.   resulted in a departure from a method of evaluation described in the FSAR and used in
                                    establishing the design bases or safety analyses.

                    Particular attention should be given to whether the possibility of a fuel assembly becoming
                    unstable or tilting following placement and grapple disengagement was considered in the
                    modi cation's §50.59 screening or evaluation.

                    If that failure mode was considered, the NRC should determine what design feature, interlock,
                    indication, procedure, or other control was credited to prevent or mitigate it and whether that
                    feature performed as intended.

                    If that failure mode was not considered, the NRC should determine whether its omission affects
                    the adequacy of the §50.59 screening or evaluation.

                    A. Broader 10 CFR 50.59 Inspection if Findings Are
                    Identi ed
                    The signi cance of the Refueling Machine §50.59 review potentially extends beyond this
                    individual modi cation.

                    During approximately the past three years, Holtec has performed a substantial program of plant
                    restoration, replacement, modi cation, testing, and con guration-control activities necessary to
                    return Palisades from decommissioning status to operation. The magnitude and complexity of
                    these activities are documented in Holtec's restart-related license amendment requests and other
                    NRC submittals.

                    The petitioner does not assert that §50.59 de ciencies exist in those other modi cations.

                    However, if NRC inspection of the Refueling Machine modi cation identi es substantive
                    de ciencies in the §50.59 screening or evaluation, design-basis review, modi cation
                    implementation, testing, or con guration control, a legitimate question would arise as to whether
                    the identi ed de ciency is isolated or indicative of a broader programmatic weakness.

                    The petitioner therefore requests that, if substantive ndings are identi ed in the Refueling
                    Machine modi cation or its §50.59 review, the NRC initiate an Event and Causal Factors
                    Inspection, Special Inspection, or other appropriate focused inspection of Palisades'
                    implementation of 10 CFR 50.59 during the restart modi cation program.

                    Such an inspection should examine a risk-informed sample of signi cant modi cations
                    completed during the approximately three-year restart effort, with particular attention to
                    modi cations affecting safety-related or safety-signi cant structures, systems, and components.

                    The inspection should evaluate, as appropriate:

                               •    10 CFR 50.59 screenings;
                               •    10 CFR 50.59 evaluations;




                                           fi                                                                 fi   fi
fi   fi
     fi        fi
          fi
          fi        fi   fi
                          fi                                                                        fi   fi
                                                fi       fi      fi   fi   fi        fi
                                                                                fi        fi   fi
                  •    design-basis veri cation;
                 •    licensing-basis identi cation;
                 •    modi cation engineering;
                 •    con guration control;
                 •    post-modi cation testing;
                 •    FSAR updating; and
                 •    management oversight of restart modi cations.
               This requested inspection is deliberately conditional.

               If NRC determines that the Refueling Machine modi cation and associated §50.59 review were
               adequate and identi es no broader programmatic concern, this additional inspection request
               would not be triggered.

               If substantive de ciencies are identi ed, however, the unprecedented scale and complexity of the
               Palisades restart modi cation program warrant NRC determination of whether the identi ed
               condition has a broader extent of condition.



               VII. EXTENT OF CONDITION AND
               CORRECTIVE ACTION
               The immediate safety concern extends beyond the affected fuel assembly.

               The unresolved issue is whether the condition that permitted one assembly to tilt could recur
               during placement of another assembly.

               The FSAR states that the Fuel Handling System incorporates interlocks, travel and load limiting
               devices, and other protective measures intended to minimize fuel mishandling or equipment
               malfunction.

               Nevertheless, the evolution progressed through placement and grapple disengagement before the
               assembly tilted.

               The NRC should therefore require an extent-of-condition evaluation addressing, at a minimum:

                 •   the newly installed Refueling Machine;
                 •   its bridge, trolley, hoist, grapple and control systems;
                 •   applicable software and control logic;
                 •   load and position indications;
                 •   interlocks and protective features;
                 •   fuel-loading procedures;
                 •   operator training;
                 •   other fuel assemblies already placed using the new equipment; and
                 •   whether the same failure mechanism could exist at another core location.
               Recovery or stabilization of the affected assembly does not resolve these questions.




fi   fi   fi    fi   fi   fi   fi   fi   fi   fi    fi                                  fi
 The cause of the condition and its potential for recurrence must be addressed independently.



VIII. NRC WORK-HOUR EXEMPTION
AND POTENTIAL ROLE OF FATIGUE
AND HUMAN PERFORMANCE
On August 12, 2026, the NRC granted Palisades Energy a one-time exemption from the normal
work-hour requirements of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(3) and (d)(7) for Operations personnel.

The exemption permitted personnel performing duties speci ed in 10 CFR 26.4(a)(1) to use the
outage minimum-days-off requirements of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(4), commencing with core-load
activities and continuing for up to 60 days or until Palisades was connected to the electrical grid,
whichever occurred rst. ML26216A290

The circumstances surrounding NRC approval of this exemption are directly relevant to the
subsequent fuel-assembly tilting event.

A. NRC's Recognition of Increased Fatigue and Human-
Error Risk
The NRC did not approve the exemption without concern.

During its review, NRC staff determined that additional clari cation and information were
required to determine whether the exemption would endanger life or property. The NRC issued
requests for con rmatory and additional information concerning, among other things,
cumulative fatigue, scheduling, fatigue limits, and continuity of operations. ML26216A290

The NRC expressly recognized that the Palisades restart differed signi cantly from a
conventional refueling outage.

The staff stated:

“the overall scope and complexity of Palisades Energy's activities differ from a typical outage”

because Palisades was concurrently restoring safety-signi cant structures, systems, and
components in addition to conducting startup activities.

The NRC further concluded:

“These additional activities could increase the amount and intensity of operator tasks or the
number and complexity of operational decisions which can contribute to an increased risk of
human error and cumulative fatigue.”




                                           fi
      fi
 fi                                             fi   fi   fi
           ML26216A290

          The NRC also recognized that startup activities were highly operationally intensive and required
          licensed operators to direct fuel load, authorize mode changes, determine operability, maintain
          Technical Speci cation compliance, and manage plant evolutions.

          The NRC noted its previous conclusion that outages increase the risk of human error because of
          higher workload, performance of more complex and infrequent tasks, and pressure to meet
          schedule goals. ML26216A290

          Of particular signi cance, the NRC expressly evaluated the changing risk pro le associated with
          commencement of core loading.

          The staff determined that the Palisades risk pro le would increase as fuel was loaded and further
          found:

          “The increased risk pro le within this exemption is compounded by the restoration of a number
          of safety-signi cant systems for safe operations and the rst-of-a-kind restart evolution.”

          The NRC concluded that this increased the potential number of tasks and decisions, together
          with the need to meet schedule pressure, which:

          “increases the potential risk of human error and fatigue.”

          ML26216A290

          The NRC further recognized that this was a rst-of-a-kind restart of a previously
          decommissioning reactor and that the operating crews included a mixture of experienced and
          less-experienced operators who might be working together for the rst time while performing
          core load, testing, inspections, surveillances, con guration changes, training, procedural
          execution and operational-readiness veri cation. ML26216A290

          B. Basis Upon Which NRC Granted the Exemption
          Despite these concerns, NRC staff concluded that Holtec's proposed mitigation strategy and
          commitments provided reasonable assurance that acute and cumulative fatigue would be
          adequately managed.

          The NRC relied upon continued maximum work-hour limitations, required rest breaks, minimum
          days off, Operations personnel's work-hour history before core load, and a required 34-hour
          break before implementation of outage work-hour controls. ML26216A290

          The NRC's nal exemption speci cally required Palisades Energy to ensure that Operations
          personnel:

               •        receive at least three days off in each successive 15-day period;
               •        remain within the maximum work-hour limits of 10 CFR 26.205(d)(1);




                                                       fi
                                                  fi
                                             fi
                                        fi
                                 fi
                        fi                                  fi
                   fi
          fi
     fi
fi                                                               fi        fi
             •    receive the 10-hour break between successive work periods required by 10 CFR
                 26.205(d)(2)(i);
            •    receive a 34-hour break in any nine-day period under 10 CFR 26.205(d)(2)(ii); and
            •    implement the mitigating strategy and commitments contained in Holtec's July 10, 2026
                 exemption request.
          The NRC concluded that these actions and commitments provided reasonable assurance that
          acute and cumulative fatigue would be adequately managed. ML26216A290

          C. Signi cance of the Subsequent Fuel-Assembly Tilting
          Event
          The subsequent fuel-assembly tilting event occurred during the very core-loading activities for
          which the exemption was granted.

          The petitioner does not assert, based upon presently available information, that fatigue caused
          the event.

          The event does, however, constitute signi cant new factual information relevant to the NRC's
          prior determination that acute and cumulative fatigue would be adequately managed during core-
          loading activities.

          Before the event occurred, NRC had already identi ed:

             •    increased workload;
             •    complex and infrequently performed activities;
             •    schedule pressure;
             •    concurrent restoration of safety-signi cant equipment;
             •      rst-of-a-kind restart conditions;
             •    mixed levels of operator experience;
             •    increased cognitive demands; and
             •    increased potential for human error and cumulative fatigue.
          The occurrence of an abnormal fuel-handling event during precisely this safety-signi cant
          evolution therefore warrants investigation of whether fatigue, workload, staf ng, scheduling,
          supervision, communications, or other human-performance factors actually caused or contributed
          to the event.

          D. Requested NRC Fatigue and Human-Performance
          Review
          The petitioner requests that NRC determine whether acute or cumulative fatigue or related
          human-performance factors caused or contributed to the fuel-assembly tilting event.

          The review should include, at a minimum:




                                              fi
                                     fi
                                fi
     fi
fi                                                                              fi
                                                                       fi
            •actual work schedules of personnel involved in directing, supervising, or performing the
            fuel-loading evolution;
       •    hours worked during the preceding 24 hours, seven days, and applicable cumulative
            periods;
       •    consecutive workdays;
       •    shift start and stop times;
       •    overtime and extended shifts;
       •    minimum break periods;
       •    days off;
       •    shift rotations;
       •    fatigue assessments;
       •    self-declarations of fatigue;
       •    supervisory behavioral observations;
       •    staf ng levels;
       •    contemporaneous workload;
       •    control-room and refueling- oor responsibilities;
       •    shift turnover records;
       •    human-performance observations;
       •    procedure use and adherence;
       •    communications, peer checks and independent veri cations associated with placement
            and release of the affected fuel assembly; and
       •    Corrective Action Program entries involving fatigue, staf ng, workload, human
            performance, or tness for duty.
     The NRC should speci cally determine whether the mitigation measures and commitments upon
     which the NRC relied in nding reasonable assurance that fatigue would be adequately managed
     were implemented as represented and were effective during the fuel-loading evolution.

     E. Requested Suspension of the Work-Hour Exemption
     Pending completion of that review, the petitioner requests that the NRC suspend the August 12,
     2026 exemption from 10 CFR 26.205(d)(3) and (d)(7), as applicable to Operations
     personnel engaged in reactor core refueling activities, and require compliance with the
     otherwise applicable work-hour controls before resumption of reactor core refueling.

     The exemption should not again be relied upon for reactor core refueling until the NRC
     independently determines:

           1.   whether acute or cumulative fatigue contributed to the fuel-assembly tilting event;

           2.   whether workload, staf ng, scheduling, schedule pressure, communications, supervision,
                or other human-performance factors contributed to the event;

           3.   whether Palisades Energy complied with the mitigation measures and commitments upon
                which NRC approval of the exemption was based; and

        4.        whether the NRC's August 12, 2026 nding of reasonable assurance regarding
                 management of acute and cumulative fatigue remains valid in light of the event.

     If NRC determines that fatigue or human-performance factors contributed to the event, NRC
     should revoke or appropriately modify the exemption and require corrective actions addressing
     those causes before authorizing further reactor core refueling operations.

     If NRC determines that fatigue and the work-hour exemption did not cause or contribute to the
     event, NRC may determine whether continued use of the exemption remains appropriate.



     IX. BASIS FOR REQUESTING AN ORDER
     BEFORE REFUELING RESUMES
     The requested enforcement action is speci c and narrowly tailored.

     The petitioner requests that NRC issue a Con rmatory Order prohibiting Palisades Energy,
     LLC from resuming reactor core refueling operations until NRC determines that:

       •    the root cause has been established;
       •    the extent of condition has been determined;

                Three related but distinct regulatory questions now require resolution.

               The rst concerns the fuel-handling event itself:

               Why did a fuel assembly tilt after it had been placed and the Refueling Machine grapple
               had been disengaged, despite an FSAR-described Fuel Handling System incorporating
               protective measures intended to provide for safe handling of fuel?

               That question implicates the corrective-action requirements of 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B,
               Criterion XVI.

               The second concerns the recently modi ed equipment:

               Did the 10 CFR 50.59 review associated with installation of the new Refueling Machine and
               upgrade of the Fuel Handling System adequately evaluate the modi cation against the
               Palisades FSAR and applicable safety analyses?

               Holtec publicly characterized installation and testing of the new Refueling Machine as a major
               project completing the upgraded Fuel Handling System.

               The subsequent occurrence of an abnormal fuel-handling event during the rst reactor core
               refueling campaign using that equipment provides a reasonable basis for NRC inspection and
               independent veri cation of the modi cation and its associated §50.59 review.

               If that review identi es substantive de ciencies, the extensive scope and complexity of
               modi cations performed during the approximately three-year Palisades restart effort warrant
               NRC determination of whether those de ciencies are isolated or represent a broader §50.59
               programmatic issue.

               The third concerns fatigue and human performance:

               Did the work schedules permitted under the August 12, 2026 work-hour exemption, or
               associated fatigue, workload, staf ng, schedule pressure, supervision, communications, or
               other human-performance factors, cause or contribute to the fuel-assembly tilting event?

               This question is particularly signi cant because the NRC itself recognized before granting the
               exemption that the Palisades restart differed from a typical outage and that concurrent restoration
               of safety-signi cant equipment could increase the intensity and complexity of operator tasks and
               thereby increase the risk of human error and cumulative fatigue. ML26216A290

               The NRC further determined that commencement of fuel loading increased the plant's risk pro le
               and that the combination of the rst-of-a-kind restart, safety-signi cant restoration work,
               increased number of tasks and decisions, and schedule pressure increased the potential risk of
               human error and fatigue. ML26216A290

               NRC nevertheless granted the exemption based upon a nding that Holtec's work-hour controls,
               mitigating strategies, and commitments provided reasonable assurance that acute and cumulative
               fatigue would be adequately managed. ML26216A290

 The significance of the Indian Point example here is procedural. The NRC did not wait for
final disposition of the entire 10 CFR 2.206 petition before addressing the requested interim
relief. Because Indian Point was in the process of restart, the Petition Review Board separately
considered the immediate-action request related to restart.

The circumstances at Palisades are comparable. Reactor core refueling was suspended
following an abnormal fuel-handling event in which a fuel assembly tilted after placement and
disengagement of the fuel-handling-machine grapple. The cause and extent of condition have
not yet been publicly established. If core loading were permitted to resume while the NRC is
processing this petition, additional fuel assemblies could be subjected to the same presently
unidentified condition before the NRC has completed its consideration of the requested
enforcement action.

Rather, I request that the NRC preserve the present condition—no further reactor core
refueling—while the Petition Review Board and NRC staff evaluate the substantive safety and
regulatory issues raised in the petition.
